title: Git-folder sync S2.1: apply scalar edits to execution-free Open restored tasks with explicit conflict refusals
outcome: Git-folder sync S2.1: apply scalar edits to execution-free Open restored tasks with explicit conflict refusals
acceptance: On the S1 two-input contract (resolved folder R plus the destination's own export basis E), changes to title, outcome and priority of execution-free Open restored tasks apply atomically through the existing Revised { authority: Project } event, with correct replay and result-graph integrity; original origins, seals and history are retained, never erased; restored Completed items stay unchanged and event-free; every other delta in this slice (an add, a delete, a prerequisite or blocker change, any other field or a lifecycle change) refuses explicitly with a named reason and is never silently dropped or partially applied

Any blocked task refuses the whole selected diff with a per-task reason naming the actual conflict (live claim, active run or admission basis, sealed or restored completion, root or parent move, unsupported delta in this slice), judged on the actual mutation and influence closure rather than a blanket refusal for an unrelated claimed task; zero changes are committed and runtime state is unchanged
Doctor verifies canonical replay of the new Revised events; repair rebuilds only declared disposable projections and preserves all durable rows and old results

completion.summary:
Git-folder sync S2.1 is landed and installed. On an enrolled destination, a resolved folder is classified task by task by the pure planner (src/task_sync/folder_plan.rs). Title, outcome and priority edits of run-free, Open, restored tasks apply as ordinary Revised{Project} planning revisions, atomically and with exact replay. Every other delta (added, deleted or unsupported fields), and every edit its task cannot take (unsupported_origin, restored_completion, lifecycle, active_run, execution_history, planning_history), refuses the whole folder with task_sync_import_conflict. That refusal names each refused task in task-id order and writes nothing. Host-local tasks the folder omits stay; the baseline records inventory changes. Doctor and repair stay healthy. There is no schema change.
